title: Copilot Studio: persistent identity (agent accounts) for agents
summary: The documented controls, preview restrictions and shared-memory warnings are supported. Microsoft now also publishes a service description with different preview timing and consumption-based account provisioning; the briefing should report that alongside the cited Frontier licensing guidance.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: Agent accounts require admin opt-in through template activation and the environment's Agent accounts setting.
claims.quote: Before users can create agents with accounts, admins must complete both steps in the following sections, in order.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationales: risk, impact
claims.claim: An agent with an account keeps one shared memory across everyone it works with.
claims.quote: The agent keeps one memory across everyone it works with, so what one person explains benefits the whole team.

claims.claim: Shared memory has no privacy boundary between users.
claims.quote: The agent is guided not to bring up one person's details with someone else, but shared memory has no privacy boundary between users.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The People card warns that shared files or chats can be summarised in responses to users without source permissions, regardless of sensitivity label.
claims.quote: Any files or chats you share can be summarized and included in the agent's responses to any user, even users without permissions to the files or chats and regardless of sensitivity label.

claims.claim: The system deletes shared memories after 28 days without anyone interacting with the agent.
claims.quote: If no one interacts with the agent for 28 days, the system automatically deletes its shared memories.

claims.claim: End users cannot opt out of shared memory in this preview.
claims.quote: No. End users can't opt out of shared memory in this preview. By using the agent, you consent to its use of shared memory.

claims.claim: The agent's memory can retain context people provide in conversations and shared chats.
claims.quote: Memory lets an agent retain what it learns in conversations, such as preferences, context, and how work gets done, and apply it in later conversations.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio also creates a separate Microsoft Entra Agent ID for each agent with an account.
claims.quote: Copilot Studio also creates a Microsoft Entra Agent ID that admins manage separately, for each agent that has an account.

claims.where: Governance controls; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Administrators can manage Copilot Studio Entra Agent IDs in the Microsoft Entra admin center.
claims.quote: You have full visibility and control in the Microsoft Entra admin center, where you can monitor authentication activity and manage the agent identity lifecycle.

claims.claim: An agent account does not automatically grant every tool permission.
claims.quote: The agent account does not automatically grant every tool permission. Check which identity a tool uses and grant only the access needed for the job.

claims.quote: You also can't change the email address for your agent after you publish the agent.

claims.quote: During this preview, you can't change the maker-based alias prefix or reporting relationship.

claims.claim: The agent's reporting relationship cannot be changed during the preview.

claims.quote: Configure supported tools and a recurrence trigger; instructions alone don't create a schedule or grant access.

claims.claim: Agents with an account support generating new documents.
claims.quote: Document editing: generating new documents is supported; editing existing documents through co-authoring isn't supported yet.

claims.quote: Policies with a tenant scope apply to all agents in all environments across the tenant.

claims.fix: Retain the cited Frontier requirements but add to Cost and licensing: 'Microsoft's Microsoft 365 Resources for Agents service description describes automatic resource provisioning rather than a manageable user licence, billed through Copilot Credits at 100 credits per agent per month plus activity. It requires consumption billing for the Copilot Studio maker. These published descriptions differ.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/office365/servicedescriptions/office-365-platform-service-description/microsoft-365-resources-for-agents and note that distinction in licensing.notes.
